context_requirements: Functional A3 adenosine receptor (ADORA3) expression; A3AR is the main adenosine receptor subtype linked to anti-tumour and anti-inflammatory transcriptional effects
Gi-coupled signalling competence (intact GNAI1/GNAI2 and downstream PI3K/NF-kB modulation)
Tumour or transformed cell context with high A3AR expression; normal/immortalised non-tumorigenic lines such as HA1E are expected to respond weakly or not at all
Adenosine transport/uptake capacity via SLC29A1 may modulate effective agonist exposure
falsifiers: No consistent decrease in proliferation-associated landmark transcripts (e.g., CCND1, MYC, CDK1, AURKA, BIRC5) at 24 h in any of the nine lines
No induction of NF-kB/AP-1 immediate-early transcripts (FOS, JUN, EGR1, NFKBIA) at 6 h in any line
Strong and uniform transcriptional response in HA1E comparable to tumour lines, arguing against A3AR-dependent, tumour-context-specific action
Absence of any apoptosis or G1-arrest signature at 24 h despite 10 micromolar exposure
Responses that are equally strong at 6 h and 24 h across all lines, contradicting the expected slow/secondary kinetics

evidence.supports: A3 adenosine receptor agonist CF102 induces apoptosis in hepatocellular carcinoma via deregulation of NF-kB and Wnt pathways
CF102, an A3AR agonist, has anti-tumour and anti-inflammatory effects in liver models, modulating GSK-3beta, NF-kB and TNF-alpha
A3AR agonist IB-MECA at 10 micromolar induces apoptosis in cardiac myocytes, supporting pro-apoptotic potential at this concentration
A3AR activation inhibits tumour cell growth via G0/G1 arrest and down-regulation of cyclin D1 and c-Myc
A3AR agonist CF101 down-regulates NF-kB-TNF-alpha signalling and inhibits proliferation in inflammatory cells
